$comment: Independent review record review_record 1.0.0 (docs/dev/independent-review-spec.md section 5.3): what one reviewer or arbiter agent (or, contracts 3.6.0, the expert agent of the optional expert slot, role expert) writes as review_record.json in its attempt folder. This schema is the single source of field names, enums and required fields: the instruction-file generator (skills/hep-authoring/scripts/review_lib/packet.py), its output example and the receipt checks all read it. Bounds, contiguity, role-dependent and basis-dependent rules the built-in validator cannot express are Python rules in contracts/review.py (record_rules). Fields the script cannot verify are marked self-reported.

packet_sha256.description: the sha256 of manifest.json in your packet folder: run `sha256sum manifest.json` there and copy the 64 hex digits

dispatch_nonce.description: the nonce= value of the second line of the dispatch message you were given, copied exactly

instructions_sha256.description: the sha256= value of the second line of the dispatch message; it equals `sha256sum instructions.md`

role.description: reviewer for a review slot, arbiter for an arbitration slot; the instruction file says which

identity.description: your agent name or session label; it must differ from the author's

context.description: fresh for a new agent context, human for a person

host.description: the host program, for example claude-code

saw_prior_conversation.description: true when any earlier conversation is visible to you; then record it and stop

host_injected.description: categories of content the host added to your context (for example: memory file, environment notes)

instruction_files_seen.description: instruction files (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, rules) visible to you, or the string unknown

reads.description: optional: read records of literature sources (hep-citations read_event; hep-citations owns their meaning)

paths_read.description: every local file you read, each with the sha256 of the whole file (`sha256sum FILE`); relative paths are relative to your attempt folder (the parent of packet/), or else to the plugin root; a file from another version or from git history is saved in work/ and cited as that copy

skim.description: one mark per skim unit in scope.json

claims.description: the claims you judged; every deep or focus unit is covered by at least one claim

evidence.description: evidence items, each with one basis and that basis's required fields

carry_forward.description: on re-review: one entry per carry_forward item in scope.json

findings.description: problems you found; value is an exact excerpt of the cited units' text in units.json

resolves.description: arbiters only: exactly one conclusion per item in items.json

limitations.description: what you could not check, and why

id.description: an identifier: a letter, then letters, digits, '_', '.', ':' or '-'

path.description: a file in your work/ folder

finding_id.description: required when mark is issue: the finding it maps to

method.description: how you tried to refute the claim

target.description: what you checked against (a file, a unit id, a URL); never empty, never the claim's own unit

value.description: the text you challenge: an exact excerpt of the cited units' text in units.json

evidence_locator.description: External: yes. Independent: it depends. Independent only when source_kind is paper, equation, table or page (a specification page inside the plugin counts), the source was read and its whole-file hash recorded, and it is not the document under review or another file the author wrote for this deliverable (docs/maintenance.md:120-121). Other locators, such as a range of lines in code, are external but not independent. Needs lines or section; a URL ref needs copy, the fetched copy saved in work/, and sha256 is the hash of that copy

sha256.description: sha256 of the whole file (for a URL: of the copy in work/)

copy.description: for a URL: the saved copy in work/

evidence_third_party.description: External: yes. Independent: yes. The expected value comes from another implementation's own algorithm, not from a library evaluating the assistant's own formula (docs/maintenance.md:122-123)

expected_from.description: which implementation's own algorithm produced the expected value

evidence_tool_output.description: External: yes. Independent: no. The output of a plugin tool

evidence_exhaustive.description: External: yes. Independent: yes. An enumeration script in work/ over a stated range

evidence_person.description: External: yes. Independent: yes. A named person or role, with the date

evidence_internal.description: External: no. Independent: no. Other units of the document; never the claim's own units or any unit within two positions of them
